symptoms.name: ransomware-note
symptoms.rationale: ransom-note symptoms: ransomware indicators plus how it got in (persistence) and what it disabled (defense evasion); event log shows the timeline

symptoms.name: ransomware-renamed-files
symptoms.rationale: mass-renamed or unopenable files are the classic encryption footprint; content scan finds notes and renamed artifacts, event log the encryption window

symptoms.name: ransomware-wallpaper
symptoms.rationale: many ransomware families replace the wallpaper with the ransom demand; treat as ransomware until proven otherwise

symptoms.name: shadow-copies-gone
symptoms.rationale: deleted shadow copies / restore points are a deliberate anti-recovery step, almost always ransomware preparation

symptoms.name: browser-homepage-hijack
symptoms.rationale: browser hijack: persistence keeps re-applying the setting, C2 covers the traffic it feeds, content scan finds the dropped component

symptoms.name: browser-redirects
phrases: takes me to a different site
symptoms.rationale: search/click redirection means an injected component or proxy setting; look for the persistence mechanism and where the traffic goes

symptoms.name: browser-popups-adware
symptoms.rationale: persistent ad injection is adware with a persistence foothold and an ad-network C2 channel

symptoms.name: unwanted-toolbar-extension
symptoms.rationale: unwanted toolbars/extensions arrive bundled with a dropper; find the extension and whatever installed it

symptoms.name: miner-slow-machine
symptoms.rationale: sudden slowness with no hardware cause is commonly a cryptominer or other resident payload; check what persists and what it talks to

symptoms.name: miner-fans-heat
symptoms.rationale: sustained fan/heat load on an idle machine points at a cryptominer burning cycles; find the mining process's persistence and pool traffic

symptoms.name: miner-cpu-gpu
symptoms.rationale: unexplained CPU/GPU load is the direct miner signature; miners persist aggressively and phone a mining pool

symptoms.name: fake-av-scareware
symptoms.rationale: scareware: fake AV warnings come from a dropped program or hijacked notifications; find the component and its persistence

symptoms.name: tech-support-scam
symptoms.rationale: a scammer with remote access may have installed persistence, remote-control tooling, and grabbed credentials — treat the whole machine as operator-touched

symptoms.name: rat-remote-control
symptoms.rationale: live remote control means an active RAT: its C2 channel, its persistence, and everything the operator could have taken (credentials)

symptoms.name: rat-webcam-microphone
symptoms.rationale: unexplained camera/microphone activation is RAT-grade surveillance; assume an implant with C2

symptoms.name: rat-ghost-activity
symptoms.rationale: flashing consoles and self-opening windows are scripted payload activity; deep-check persistence, C2, and the event timeline

symptoms.name: unexpected-remote-tools
symptoms.rationale: legitimate remote-admin tools the owner didn't install are a favorite attacker foothold — check when they arrived and what account used them

symptoms.name: stolen-passwords-accounts
symptoms.rationale: account takeovers usually trace back to an infostealer on the machine: find the stealer, its persistence, its exfil channel, and the phish that delivered it

symptoms.name: keylogger-suspected
symptoms.rationale: keylogger suspicion: credential-access tooling with persistence and an exfil channel

symptoms.name: banking-fraud
phrases: credit card charges i didn't make
symptoms.rationale: financial fraud from this machine suggests a banking trojan or infostealer: web-inject components, credential theft, and C2

symptoms.name: clicked-phishing-link
symptoms.rationale: phishing-click aftermath: check the mail residue for the lure, then whether anything landed (persistence) or calls out (C2)

symptoms.name: opened-malicious-attachment
symptoms.rationale: opened-attachment aftermath: the lure lives in mail residue, the dropped payload in content scan, its foothold in persistence

symptoms.name: entered-credentials-on-fake-page
phrases: signed in on a weird site
symptoms.rationale: credentials handed to a fake page: assume account compromise, hunt for follow-on access and the phish that started it

symptoms.name: macro-enabled-document
symptoms.rationale: an enabled macro is direct code execution from a document: find the doc, the dropped payload, and its persistence

symptoms.name: outbound-spam-from-account
phrases: everyone got an email from me
friends got weird messages from me
symptoms.rationale: outbound spam in the user's name means account or machine compromise: mailbox abuse, stolen credentials, or a local spam bot

symptoms.name: malicious-inbox-rules
symptoms.rationale: hidden inbox/forwarding rules are the signature of business email compromise — attacker-held credentials quietly diverting mail

symptoms.name: account-lockouts
symptoms.rationale: repeated lockouts usually mean password-guessing against the account — the event log holds the source

symptoms.name: password-changed-itself
symptoms.rationale: a password changed without the owner is post-compromise account control; check who changed it and what else that session did

symptoms.name: failed-logon-noise
symptoms.rationale: failed-logon noise is credential attack traffic; the event log identifies the source, target accounts, and whether anything succeeded

symptoms.name: unknown-startup-program
phrases: launches on its own at boot
symptoms.rationale: an unrecognized startup entry IS a persistence finding — enumerate every autostart location, not just the one the user saw

symptoms.name: strange-scheduled-task
symptoms.rationale: scheduled tasks are a top persistence mechanism; check task actions and creation times against the event log

symptoms.name: unknown-service
symptoms.rationale: unrecognized services are persistence with SYSTEM privileges; service-install events pin the arrival time

symptoms.name: keeps-coming-back
phrases: removed it but it came back
symptoms.rationale: self-resurrecting malware has a persistence mechanism the removal missed — possibly WMI, a watchdog pair, or boot-level; go deep

symptoms.name: antivirus-disabled
symptoms.rationale: security tooling doesn't turn itself off — deliberate defense evasion implies an active payload it was protecting

symptoms.name: admin-tools-blocked
symptoms.rationale: blocked admin tools are classic self-protection: policy keys set by malware to survive inspection; check boot-level hiding too

symptoms.name: security-tool-sabotage
symptoms.rationale: malware killing or starving security tools is active interference — expect a resident component with watchdog behavior

symptoms.name: suspicious-network-traffic
symptoms.rationale: unexplained traffic is potential C2 — map live connections to processes and find what persists them

symptoms.name: firewall-alerts
symptoms.rationale: firewall alerts or self-added rules show something trying to reach out or opening a listening door

symptoms.name: data-exfiltration
symptoms.rationale: sustained outbound volume looks like data theft: identify the channel, and content-scan for staging archives left behind

symptoms.name: dns-hosts-tampering
symptoms.rationale: DNS/hosts/proxy tampering redirects the whole machine through attacker infrastructure — a persistence-backed man-in-the-middle

symptoms.name: internet-degraded
phrases: wifi is slow on this machine
symptoms.rationale: single-machine network slowness can be traffic-hungry malware (proxy, bot, miner) — worth a C2 and persistence pass

symptoms.name: crashes-bluescreens
symptoms.rationale: boot-time crashes can be a badly-written rootkit or bootkit fighting the OS — inspect boot configuration, drivers, and crash events

symptoms.name: hidden-or-missing-files
symptoms.rationale: vanished files are either hidden (rootkit / USB shortcut worms set +h), encrypted-and-moved (ransomware), or permission-blocked (ACL tampering)

symptoms.name: system-acting-possessed
phrases: has a mind of its own
symptoms.rationale: vague 'possessed' behavior with settings that fight back suggests a resident component with self-defense — check deep, including boot

symptoms.name: rdp-enabled-unexpectedly
symptoms.rationale: RDP enabled without the owner is attacker access being set up (or already used) — the event log shows who connected and when

symptoms.name: unknown-admin-account
phrases: extra account on the login screen
symptoms.rationale: an attacker-created account is both persistence and privilege — account-management events and permission changes tell the story

symptoms.name: usb-removable-media
symptoms.rationale: USB worms hide the real files and plant shortcuts/autoruns; scan for the dropped payload and its persistence

symptoms.name: webshell-server
symptoms.rationale: server-side compromise: content-scan web roots for shells, check persistence and the accounts/permissions the shell touched

symptoms.name: file-permission-tampering
phrases: permission denied on my own files
symptoms.rationale: self-changing permissions are ACL tampering — used to lock the owner out or to protect malware files from deletion

symptoms.name: spam-popup-notifications
symptoms.rationale: notification/calendar spam is usually a granted browser permission or a resident adware component pushing it

symptoms.name: process-impersonation
symptoms.rationale: look-alike or unexpected processes are payloads hiding in plain sight — trace their image paths, persistence, and network use
